reviewed.attack: Searched Zenodo (API, type=dataset: harmonica, melodica, mandolin, bouzouki, free reed, isolated notes, single notes, plucked string recordings), archive.org advancedsearch (audio and texts; sample packs, soundfonts) and Wikimedia Commons (API rate-limited with HTTP 429, so the ordinary Special:Search HTML and action=render file pages were used) and read each candidate's licence on its own record.
reviewed.finding: The negative claim no longer holds for bouzouki: Wikimedia Commons has four isolated open-course notes of an Irish bouzouki (Tuning-Sound-G/-d/-a/-dd-Bouzouki.ogg, 24 August 2019, author SoylentGreen, 'Own work', CC BY-SA 4.0 as read on each file page) plus scale recordings by the same author under the same licence; these are redistributable with attribution and share-alike on the audio. Harmonica: Commons has 'Bending Mundharmonika.ogg' (draw bends, Matthias.Gruber 2006, GFDL 1.2+ and CC BY-SA 3.0) and six short public-domain clips from pdsounds.org (Harmonica 02-07, mastermesh, 22 kHz MP3 origin, content not checked as single notes); neither is a clean isolated-note set. Mandolin: no isolated-note set; archive.org item 'G-Town Church Sampling Project' (Tobias Marberger) states it contains mandolin samples under CC Sampling Plus 1.0 (contents not listed: the zip listing host was refused); Philharmonia remains the best mandolin reference (private). Melodica: only an Electra-Melodica (an electro-acoustic 1967 Hohner variant, CC BY-SA 4.0) recording and pronunciation files; nothing usable. Zenodo has no audio for any of the four (its 'harmonica' and 'mandolin' hits are 3-D models); Good-sounds (CC BY 4.0) covers 12 orchestral instruments, none of these.
reviewed.suggested_rewording: No redistributable set of isolated notes was found for harmonica, melodica or mandolin on Zenodo, archive.org or Wikimedia Commons (Freesound not reachable). For the Irish bouzouki, Wikimedia Commons has four CC BY-SA 4.0 open-course single notes (G, d, a, d') by one contributor, usable as redistributable references with attribution and share-alike.

missing_claims.claim: JUCE 9 (9.0.0, 2026-07-21; 9.0.5, 2026-11-02) is the current major release and carries the same parser hardening as 8.0.17-security; choosing the JUCE 8 maintenance line is a decision that needs a recorded reason (and switching later changes the Linux dependency list: libxi-dev becomes required in 9.0.0).
missing_claims.why_it_matters: The plan pins a framework for five plug-ins; the EULA, dependency recipe and API differ between majors.
missing_claims.evidence: git ls-remote and CHANGE_LIST.md / BREAKING_CHANGES.md at 9.0.5 (this round).

missing_claims.claim: numpy 2.5.x and scipy 1.18.x require Python 3.12 or later.
missing_claims.why_it_matters: CI runner Python versions and setup-python pins must match.

missing_claims.claim: Reference downloads need hosts outside the current allow-list (Philharmonia zips on philharmonia-assets.s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com; archive.org item downloads redirect to ia*.us.archive.org; Freesound).
missing_claims.why_it_matters: An implementer's bounded search and CI fetch steps will fail without them.
missing_claims.evidence: Philharmonia page links; archive.org zip listing refused (this round).

missing_claims.claim: The cost of the reed model per sample (one Su table lookup, one division, a few multiply-adds per reed) times the number of simultaneously sounding reeds (an accordion Master register with chords is several tens of reeds) and any oversampling factor sets the CPU budget; no measurement exists yet.
missing_claims.why_it_matters: Oversampling choice and voice limits; the spike ran in pure Python and says nothing about C++ cost.
missing_claims.evidence: S03 code structure; no benchmark in the register.
